# @bwilliamson/mdcp-core

<!-- mdcp-shard: start ../../docs/client-core/about.md -->

## About @bwilliamson/mdcp-core

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@bwilliamson/mdcp-core.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@bwilliamson/mdcp-core)

The **programmatic core library** for the [MarkDown Context Protocol (MDCP)](https://github.com/betsalel-williamson/mdcp). It compiles sharded Markdown guides and validates their structure. From the compiled output it also builds the registry of section links (`refs.json`).

Use this package when you need compile, validation, and refs APIs in scripts, CI, editors, or other tools **without** shelling out to the CLI.

### Not the CLI or the Agent Skill

- **This library:** the TypeScript/Node API from `@bwilliamson/mdcp-core` on npm
- **CLI:** the command-line wrapper around this library, [`@bwilliamson/mdcp-cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@bwilliamson/mdcp-cli)
- **Agent Skill:** the host instructions an agent loads for `/mdcp`, installed as [Get started](../../README.md#get-started) in the project README describes

`@bwilliamson/mdcp-cli` depends on this package, so install `@bwilliamson/mdcp-core` directly only when you need the programmatic API. The Agent Skill is a separate install: this library doesn't depend on it, and installing the skill does **not** install this library.

### Requirements

- Node.js **>= 18.0.0**

### Install

```bash
npm install @bwilliamson/mdcp-core
```

### Stability

Before **1.0.0**, exported functions, types, the `mdcp.config.json` schema and compile output can change in any `0.x.y` release, under the [pre-1.0 policy](../../DEVELOPERS.md#pre-10-policy-0xy). [Stability](../mdcp-cli/README.md#stability) in the CLI README says what to read before upgrading.

## Quick example

This script compiles every guide and writes the outputs, then regenerates the refs registry from them. Run it from the directory that holds `docs/mdcp.config.json`.

```typescript
import { join } from 'node:path';
import {
  loadConfig,
  resolveDocsRoot,
  resolveOutputPath,
  compileGuideResults,
  compileGuidesFromResults,
  writeCompiledGuidesFromResults,
  refsOutputTexts,
  resolveRefsPath,
  genRefsFromCompiled,
} from '@bwilliamson/mdcp-core';

const config = loadConfig('docs/mdcp.config.json', process.cwd());
const docsRoot = join(process.cwd(), 'docs');

const options = {
  guidesRoot: resolveDocsRoot(config, docsRoot),
  compileOrder: config.compileOrder,
  banner: config.banner,
  guides: config.guides,
  docsRoot,
  config,
};
const results = compileGuideResults(options);
writeCompiledGuidesFromResults(results, options, resolveOutputPath(config, docsRoot));

const compiled = compileGuidesFromResults(results, options);
const outputs = refsOutputTexts(results, options);
const refsPath = resolveRefsPath(docsRoot, config.outputDir, config.refs.registryFile);
genRefsFromCompiled(compiled, refsPath, outputs);
```

In CI, call `checkRefsRegistry(compiled, refsPath, outputs)` in place of `genRefsFromCompiled`. It returns `ok: false` when the registry on disk is missing or stale. The [Compile API](#compile-api) lists the fields of each result and says when compile writes the monolith, the one file that top-level `outputFile` names. The [Config API](#config-api) says which base each path resolves from.

## Config API

| Export                                                                                 | Purpose                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `loadConfig(path, configBase)`                                                         | Load and validate `mdcp.config.json` (`path` is resolved from `configBase`)      |
| `resolveOutputPath`, `resolveRefsPath`, `resolveGuideDir`, `resolveUnderOutputDir`     | Path resolvers for docs root and `outputDir`                                     |
| `defaultGuideOutputFile`, `effectiveGuideOutputFile`                                   | A guide's default output file name, and its `compile.outputFile` or that default |
| `resolveDocsRoot(config, docsRoot)`                                                    | The docs root, which is `docsRoot` as given                                      |
| `resolveGuideLinkBase(config, docsRoot, name, compileOrderLength, compile)`            | The output a publish output links to for a guide                                 |
| `getGuideConfig`, `guideScanDirs`, `shardLintPaths`                                    | In-scope guide fileset and shard lint helpers                                    |
| `MdcpConfigSchema`, `MdcpConfig`, `MdcpConfigInput`, `GuideConfig`, `GuideConfigInput` | Zod schema and types                                                             |
| `DEFAULT_COMPILE_HOOKS`, `resolveCompileHooks`                                         | Default built-in hook pipeline and guide-level resolution                        |

`resolveGuideLinkBase` returns the guide's `compile.outputFile` when the guide sets one. Without one, it returns the monolith when the config has one, and the guide's compiled guide otherwise. Despite its name, the result is the [link base](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#when-it-runs) of only the assembly that writes that file. A guide in the monolith has one link base per document, and its own compiled guide rebases on its own path rather than on the monolith this returns.

### Path resolution: `configBase` vs docs root

| Concern                    | Base                          | Example                                                                          |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Finding `mdcp.config.json` | `configBase` (invocation dir) | `--config docs/mdcp.config.json` → `<repo>/docs/mdcp.config.json`                |
| Guide shards (default)     | Docs root (`--docs-root`)     | `resolveGuideDir('features', config, docsRoot)` → absolute `<docsRoot>/features` |

`resolveOutputPath` and `resolveRefsPath` resolve a generated path with `resolveUnderOutputDir(docsRoot, outputDir, file)`. [Resolution bases](../mdcp-cli/README.md#resolution-bases) in Config essentials gives the base of `outputDir` and of each generated path.

```typescript
import { loadConfig, resolveGuideDir } from '@bwilliamson/mdcp-core';

const config = loadConfig('docs/mdcp.config.json', process.cwd());
const featuresDir = resolveGuideDir('features', config, join(process.cwd(), 'docs'));
```

Pass `process.cwd()` as `configBase` for `loadConfig`. Pass the docs root as `docsRoot` to `resolveGuideDir`, `resolveOutputPath`, and `resolveRefsPath`.

`resolveGuideDir` and `guideScanDirs` return absolute paths. A relative `docsRoot` such as `docs` resolves against the process cwd. The CLI runs markdownlint-cli2 and Vale with the docs root as their cwd, where a relative `docs/features` would name `docs/docs/features`, a directory that doesn't exist.

`shardLintPaths(config, docsRoot)` returns paths for markdownlint-cli2 run with the docs root as its cwd, as `mdcp lint` and `mdcp check` run it. From another cwd, the relative paths match the wrong files or none. Without `lint.markdownlint.shardsGlobs`, it returns one glob per guide directory, as [In-scope guide fileset](../mdcp-cli/README.md#in-scope-guide-fileset) describes, and `**/*.{md,markdown}` for a guide whose directory is the docs root. A relative glob that would start with `!`, `#` or `:` gets a leading `./`, so markdownlint-cli2 doesn't read it as a negation or a literal path. Use `guideScanDirs` for the directories themselves.

With `shardsGlobs`, it returns each entry as written, negated entries included, with two exceptions. A `.` entry becomes `**`. An entry that starts with `../` gets the escaped absolute directory those segments name in their place, then `/**` when the entry is a directory, and a negated one gets `**` in front.

`loadConfig` validates the file with `MdcpConfigSchema` and fills the top-level defaults, such as `outputDir`, `banner`, `sourceTags`, `scan`, `backup`, `refs` and `review`. A key inside an omitted optional object, such as `lint`, `lint.links`, `vale` or a guide's `compile`, is `undefined` after loading, and the code that reads it applies the documented default. Config essentials lists the output layout and its defaults under [Path layout](../mdcp-cli/README.md#path-layout). [Source tags and default banner](../../docs/features/source-tags-and-banner.md) gives the default banner text and the per-guide `compile.includeBanner` and `compile.sourceTags` keys.

#### Publish outputs and link paths

Guides with `compile.outputFile` publish outside the shard tree (npm READMEs, `DEVELOPERS.md`, and similar).

After the cross-guide and intra-guide rewrites, compile resolves the `../` links a shard still has and writes them relative to the guide's [link base](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#when-it-runs). [Publish-relative exclusions](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#publish-relative-exclusions) lists the links it leaves as written, such as a path that leads to no file. A guide doesn't need path-prefix config for this. [Link passes](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/link-passes.md) lists the passes in order, and [Publish-relative link rewriting](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md) has examples from MDCP's own docs.

### `compile.hooks`

`resolveCompileHooks(compile)` returns the list of hooks a guide runs, which is `DEFAULT_COMPILE_HOOKS` when `compile.hooks` is omitted. [Configuration](#configuration) in the hooks overview covers the config keys.

### `compile.crossGuideLinks`

Assembly-time cross-guide link options on the **compiling** guide (not a compile hook):

- **`ignoreGuides`**: `string[]` of guide names. Links from the compiling guide to shards of a listed guide keep source `.md` paths instead of rewriting to `#slug` targets, except where a link to a shard the compiling guide stitches takes its in-document anchor, as [ignoreGuides](#ignoreguides) says.

See [Cross-guide link rewriting](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/cross-guide-links.md).

## Compile API

| Export                                                                           | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `compileGuides`, `compileGuideResults`                                           | Stitch shards into compiled guide text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `compileGuideResultsWithContext`                                                 | The results of `compileGuideResults`, with the guide link index, the shard cache it built and the shards each guide compiles, its manifest's and those the [linked-shard walk](../../docs/features/manifest-compile-order.md#linked-shards-and-the-file-name-fallback) finds (`linkedFilesByGuide`) |
| `compileGuidesFromResults`                                                       | What `compileGuides` returns, from results already compiled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `writeCompiledGuides`, `writeCompiledGuidesFromResults`                          | Write compiled guides and the optional monolith to disk, the second from results already compiled                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `compiledOutputDocuments`                                                        | Each file compile writes, with the text written there                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `buildGuideLinkIndex`                                                            | The [guide link index](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/cross-guide-links.md#guide-link-index) alone, with the shard cache it filled                                                                                                                                                            |
| `createShardCache`, `loadShardSnapshot`                                          | A cache of shard reads that compile and link lint can share                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `writeOutputFile`, `resolveBackupPath`                                           | Opt-in backup before overwrite; backup path resolver                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `resolveBackupOptions`                                                           | Merge config and CLI backup settings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `WriteOutputBackupOptions`                                                       | Backup options type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `sectionFiles`, `processSection`, `assembleGuide`                                | Lower-level assemble pipeline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `formatCompileTitle`, `extractFirstHeading`, …                                   | Optional `compile.title` injection and deduplication                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `demoteHeadings`, `stripAboutThisGuideHeading`, …                                | Heading transforms                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `rewriteCrossGuideFileLinks`, `rewriteIntraGuideFileLinks`, `slugForSectionFile` | Two of the [link passes](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/link-passes.md), and the slug of a shard's demoted first heading, before guide numbering                                                                                                                                              |
| `stripExplicitAnchorMarkers`                                                     | The [stripAnchors](#stripanchors) transform on a string                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `registerCompileHook`, `applyCompileHooks`                                       | Extension hooks (`stripAnchors`, `inlineInserts`, …)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

`compileGuideResults` returns one result per guide. Its `text` is the guide's compiled guide, with links and source tags relative to that file. The monolith is the one file that top-level `outputFile` names, and it stitches each guide without `compile.outputFile`. A guide in the monolith also has a [copy there](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#when-it-runs), and its result stores that copy in `monolithText`, with paths and section slugs as the monolith has them.

A result's `knownSlugs` holds the section slugs of `text`, the slug of each section it stitches, such as a `FIND-*` finding id or a declared `{#id}`. `monolithKnownSlugs` does the same for `monolithText`: the section slugs of every copy in the monolith, a set each copy shares. Broken-link marking and `lintLinks` accept a `#fragment` that matches one of these slugs or a heading, as [BROKEN LINK marker](../../docs/features/link-validation.md#broken-link-marker) says. A fragment on a link from another output has to match a heading there, so neither set counts for it, as [Validation phases](../../docs/features/link-validation.md#validation-phases) says.

`compiledOutputDocuments(results, options)` returns each file that compile writes from the same results and options: every compiled guide in `compileOrder`, then the monolith when the config sets top-level `outputFile` and at least one guide is stitched into it. The monolith's path is the config's `outputFile` under `outputDir`, the path that `resolveOutputPath` gives and the CLI passes to `writeCompiledGuidesFromResults`. Each entry has the absolute `path` and the `text` written there, banner included, so a line number in the text is a line of the file. A compiled guide's entry names its result in `guide`. The monolith's entry lists each guide's copy in `copies`, with the line the copy starts on. `lintLinks` reads the outputs through it, and so does `refsOutputTexts`, which gives the refs registry each output's text.

When top-level `outputFile` is set, `compileGuides` returns the monolith text, which leaves out guides with `compile.outputFile`. Otherwise it returns every compiled guide joined in the order of `compileOrder`. `compileGuidesFromResults` does the same from results, and it stitches the monolith from each result's `monolithText`. `writeCompiledGuides` writes each compiled guide to its output path. It also writes the monolith when you pass its path and at least one guide has no `compile.outputFile`.

`writeOutputFile` writes compile targets. Default: overwrite. When `backup.enabled` is true, it moves an existing file to the path that [Backup path layout](../../docs/features/compile-output-backup.md#backup-path-layout) gives before writing. Pass `backup` on `CompileOptions` or resolve via `resolveBackupOptions(config, cliOverrides)`.

When `compile.title` is set, `assembleGuide` injects a `##` heading followed by a blank line before the first section. [Feature settings](../mdcp-cli/README.md#feature-settings) in Config essentials says which spec covers each feature's config keys, `backup` included.

### Locale packs

A [locale pack](#locale-pack) holds the words compile writes and reads in prose, such as the BROKEN LINK marker and the line-range words of `codeEvidence`. Compile and `lintLinks` use the en-US pack, the only one `getLocalePack` resolves. `buildSlugRegistry` and `stripAboutThisGuideHeading` take a pack as an argument, and `markBrokenLinks` and `lintCompiledLinks` take one as their `locale` option. Each uses en-US without one.

| Export                                                                                      | Purpose                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `getLocalePack(id)`, `listLocalePackIds`, `DEFAULT_LOCALE_ID`, `enUS`                       | Resolve a built-in pack by its BCP 47 id, `en-US` by default |
| `createLocalePack(options)`, `createBrokenLinksCopy`, `createInsertsCopy`, `formatTemplate` | Build a pack from message templates                          |

## Refs and validation API

### Refs (cross-links)

| Export                                                         | Purpose                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `headingTextToPlain`, `githubSlugify`, `buildSlugRegistry`     | GitHub heading slugs via github-slugger                                 |
| `genRefsFromCompiled`, `readRefsRegistry`, `checkRefsRegistry` | `refs.json` lifecycle                                                   |
| `refsOutputTexts`, `buildRefsRegistry`                         | Each compiled output for the registry, and the registry built in memory |
| `resolveRefsPath`, `writeRefsRegistry`                         | Path and I/O helpers                                                    |

#### `refsOutputTexts(results, options)`

Returns each file compile writes from `results`, in the order `compiledOutputDocuments` gives them. Each entry has `file`, the path relative to `options.docsRoot` with `/` separators, and `text`, what compile writes there, banner included. A compiled guide's entry also names its guide in `guideName`. Pass the list as the last argument of `genRefsFromCompiled(compiledText, registryPath, outputs)` and `checkRefsRegistry(compiledText, registryPath, outputs)`. The registry then has an `outputs` entry for each file, with that file's headings slugged on their own and each `line` counted in that file. `buildRefsRegistry(compiledText, outputs)` returns the same registry without writing it.

The registry's top-level `headings` and `slugs` come from `compiledText` alone, the text `compileGuidesFromResults` returns. Without `outputs`, the registry has no `outputs` field. `checkRefsRegistry` compares the file with the registry its own arguments give, so a registry written with `outputs` is stale to a check without them, and the reverse. [Registry contents](../mdcp-cli/README.md#registry-contents) lists the fields.

#### `resolveRefsPath(docsRoot, outputDir, registryFile)`

Resolves the on-disk path for the refs registry. Implemented via the same `outputDir`-relative helper as `resolveOutputPath`. Pass the docs root (the CLI `--docs-root` value).

- `outputDir` is relative to `docsRoot`.
- `registryFile` resolves by the rule in [Path layout](../mdcp-cli/README.md#path-layout) (default `.caches/refs.json`).

```typescript
resolveRefsPath('/docs', '_build', '.caches/refs.json');
// → /docs/_build/.caches/refs.json

resolveRefsPath('/docs', '.', 'refs.json');
// → /docs/refs.json
```

#### Heading slugs (github-slugger)

`githubSlugify`, `headingTextToPlain`, and `buildSlugRegistry` derive `#fragment` targets from compiled headings using [`github-slugger`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/github-slugger), which matches the anchors GitHub renders for headings. GFM does not define auto-generated heading IDs. Treat github-slugger parity as the contract.

| Export               | Purpose                                              |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `headingTextToPlain` | Strip ids and inline markup before slugging          |
| `githubSlugify`      | Single-heading slug via github-slugger               |
| `buildSlugRegistry`  | Document-wide slugs; duplicates get numeric suffixes |

`buildSlugRegistry` reads only headings outside fenced code blocks, which it finds with the [fence scan](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/fence-scan.md). A `# comment` in a shell example doesn't get a slug, and it doesn't change the guide that later headings belong to. Compile numbers [section slugs](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/section-slugs.md) through the same reader, so a rewritten section link and the registry agree, apart from the limits that page lists. Heading demotion, in compile and in `demoteHeadings`, leaves each line that the same scan reads as code as written. [Fence scan limits](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/fence-scan.md#fence-scan-limits) says when demotion and `buildSlugRegistry` can disagree about a shard.

```typescript
import { githubSlugify, headingTextToPlain } from '@bwilliamson/mdcp-core';

headingTextToPlain('**Authored GFM** `{#gfm}`');
// → 'Authored GFM'

githubSlugify('Preprocessor / templating (out of scope)');
// → 'preprocessor--templating-out-of-scope'

githubSlugify('`--config` vs `--docs-root`');
// → '--config-vs---docs-root'
```

CLI authoring rules: [Cross-links and refs — heading slugs](../mdcp-cli/README.md#heading-slugs-github-rules).

## Shard and peers API

### Shard (split)

| Export                           | Purpose                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `shardFromMonolith`, `runMdTree` | Split a source document into guide directories |

`shardFromMonolith` reads a source document such as a legacy README, not the compiled monolith. It splits the source at its H1 headings. Each `mappings` entry either picks H1 sections for one guide (`h1Index` or `mergeH1Indices`) and splits them as [Map the document to guides](../mdcp-cli/README.md#map-the-document-to-guides) describes, or copies an existing directory (`directoryPath`). `mdcp shard` builds the mappings from each guide's `source` config.

### Peer tools

| Export                      | Purpose                                                           |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `findPeerBinary`, `runPeer` | Locate and run host-repo linters (`markdownlint-cli2`, `vale`, …) |

`findPeerBinary(name, cwd)` returns `source: 'local'` for a `node_modules/.bin` binary found from `cwd` upward, `'path'` for one on PATH, and `found: false` otherwise. `runPeer` then skips the tool with an info line unless `require` is set, which makes a missing tool an error. [Peer linters](../../docs/features/design-constraints/peer-linters.md) is the policy.

## Compile hooks

Per-shard transforms run during `assembleGuide` **before** sections are stitched. Hooks receive each shard body after heading demotion and preamble stripping. The diagram below shows the steps around the hooks.

Hooks assemble [authored GFM](#authored-gfm). They don't do variable substitution or template logic. See [Preprocessor / templating (out of scope)](../../docs/features/design-constraints/preprocessor-templating.md#preprocessor--templating-out-of-scope).

### Architecture

```text
assembleGuide (per guide, once for each document it is written to)
  │
  ├─ for each shard (manifest order, then linked shards)
  │    ├─ processSection (demote headings, strip about-this-guide)
  │    ├─ applyCompileHooks (named hooks from config, in order)
  │    ├─ mark the paths codeEvidence rebased
  │    ├─ cross-guide pass (automatic when link index present, marks what it writes)
  │    ├─ rewriteIntraGuideFileLinks (same-guide links, from the shard directory)
  │    └─ rewritePublishRelativeLinks (every guide, relative to its link base, marks what it writes)
  │
  ├─ stitch → stripAnchors (default) → intra-guide .md → unmark
  │
  └─ markBrokenLinks → realignTables (the last step)
```

**Guide link index**: `compileGuideResults` builds it once from every guide in `compileOrder`, and the cross-guide pass reads it. [Guide link index](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/cross-guide-links.md#guide-link-index) says which shards have an entry.

**Per-assembly hook state**: mutable `hookState` on `CompileHookContext` (such as `inlineInserts` counters and first-anchor map) shared across shard invocations within one assembly. Each assembly starts with fresh `hookState`, and a guide in the monolith has one assembly for each document, as [When it runs](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#when-it-runs) says. So every hook it runs, a registered custom hook included, sees each of its shards twice, and a hook with side effects beyond its return value repeats them.

The Features Guide's [Compile pipeline](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/index.md) specifies the assembly steps that aren't hooks, and the rules they share with the hooks. Its [Path lookup order](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/path-lookup-order.md) gives the directories each hook and pass tries when it follows a link to a file.

### Extension pattern

A custom hook runs only in a process that registers it with `registerCompileHook` before it calls `compileGuideResults` or `compileGuides`. Importing the core registers the built-in hooks and `identity`, which returns the body unchanged. The mdcp CLI doesn't load a custom hook, so `mdcp compile` and `mdcp check` compile without one. Register yours in your own build script:

```typescript
import { registerCompileHook } from '@bwilliamson/mdcp-core';

registerCompileHook('myHook', (ctx) => {
  return ctx.body.replace(/TODO/g, 'DONE');
});
```

Then list it in the array form of `compile.hooks` next to the built-in hooks the guide keeps, such as `["stripAnchors", "codeEvidence", "inlineInserts", "myHook"]`. [Explicit override](../../docs/features/default-compile-hooks.md#explicit-override) says the array replaces the default pipeline, so it has to list them.

Compile skips any name in `compile.hooks` that has no registered hook, and it doesn't warn. A misspelled name, such as `codeEvidense`, compiles as if the list left it out, and no check reports it. Registering a hook under a name already in use replaces that hook, a built-in one included.

A hook gets a `CompileHookContext` and returns the new body. Assembly always sets `hookState`, and passes `{}` as `config` when the caller doesn't give one. `compileGuideResults` sets every other field, and `scopeRoot` only when the guide sets `compile.scopeRoot`. A direct `assembleGuide` call sets `outputFile`, `outputBasename`, `scopeRoot` and `linkIndex` only when its options give them.

| Field            | Value                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `body`           | The shard body, after heading demotion, preamble stripping and the hooks listed before this one                                     |
| `guideName`      | The configured name of the guide being compiled                                                                                     |
| `filename`       | The shard's file name                                                                                                               |
| `sourceFile`     | The shard's absolute path                                                                                                           |
| `config`         | The config the caller passed as `CompileOptions.config` (an `MdcpConfigInput`), or `{}`                                             |
| `outputFile`     | Optional. The absolute path of the guide's [link base](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#when-it-runs) |
| `outputBasename` | Optional. The file name of `outputFile`                                                                                             |
| `scopeRoot`      | Optional. The absolute `compile.scopeRoot`, unset when the guide doesn't set it                                                     |
| `hookState`      | State that the hook calls of one assembly share, from one shard to the next. Always set, though the type marks it optional          |
| `linkIndex`      | Optional. The [guide link index](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/cross-guide-links.md#guide-link-index)                        |

Hook implementations should be **pure on `ctx.body`** except when intentionally using shared `hookState`. Leave unmatched links unchanged.

### Configuration

Built-in hooks run by default, so omit `compile.hooks` for the common case. [Default compile hooks](../../docs/features/default-compile-hooks.md#configuration) gives the forms `compile.hooks` takes to turn a hook off or replace the list. Per-hook settings go under `guides[].compile.hooksConfig`, as [inlineInserts config](#inlineinserts-config) shows, and the [config API](#compilehooks) covers `resolveCompileHooks`. [stripAnchors purpose](#stripanchors-purpose) says what `compile.stripAnchors` does.

For manifest compile order and `compile.sectionsHeading`, see [Manifest compile order](../../docs/features/manifest-compile-order.md).

### Built-in hooks

- **`stripAnchors`**: per shard. [stripAnchors](#stripanchors): removes `{#id}` markers outside code, and every marker on a heading line.
- **`codeEvidence`**: per shard. [codeEvidence](#codeevidence): repo source links → `#L` fragments.
- **`inlineInserts`**: per shard. [inlineInserts](#inlineinserts): inline captioned insert libraries.

Assembly also runs the [link passes](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/link-passes.md), which aren't hooks. Its last step, after broken-link marking, is [table re-alignment](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/tables-after-link-rewriting.md), which prints an aligned table again once its links change width.

<!-- mdcp-shard: end ../../docs/client-core/compile-hooks/index.md -->

<!-- mdcp-shard: start ../../docs/client-core/compile-hooks/strip-anchors.md -->

## stripAnchors

Specification for the `stripAnchors` compile hook. The [Spec-to-test map](../../DEVELOPERS.md#spec-to-test-map) names the tests behind this spec.

### stripAnchors purpose

The hook removes `{#id}` anchor markers from each shard body. With `compile.stripAnchors` (default `true`), the same strip runs once more on the stitched guide.

A marker goes with the whitespace before it on the same line. When a marker opens a line's text, the whitespace after it goes instead, and the line keeps its indent. The strip drops a line that contains only a marker, and when that line opens the text or follows a blank line, the blank line right after it goes too.

### stripAnchors heading lines

A line that mdcp reads as a heading, an ATX heading at column 0, loses every marker, even inside a fenced code block or a code span. Heading slugs drop every marker from a title and skip the lines that the [fence scan](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/fence-scan.md) reads as code. The scan ignores HTML and can misread a fence there, so stripping every heading line keeps a marker off a rendered heading even then.

To show the syntax on a heading inside a fenced example, start the heading line one to three spaces in. mdcp doesn't read that line as a heading. The strip treats it as fenced text and keeps its marker. Outside a fence the same line is prose, and its marker goes.

### stripAnchors code

On any other line, a `{#id}` inside a fenced code block or an inline code span stays. The hook finds both with the [fence scan](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/fence-scan.md).

### stripAnchors limits

The strip reads an indented code block as prose, as the fence scan does. It removes a marker there unless the marker is inside a code span on its line. The hook runs the scan without the blockquote text, so a fence behind `>` is prose to it too, and a marker there goes unless a code span on its line holds it. Where the [fence scan limits](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/fence-scan.md#fence-scan-limits) misread a fence or shift the pairing of code spans, the strip can drop a quoted marker or keep a prose one.

<!-- mdcp-shard: end ../../docs/client-core/compile-hooks/strip-anchors.md -->

<!-- mdcp-shard: start ../../docs/client-core/compile-hooks/code-evidence.md -->

## codeEvidence

Specification for the `codeEvidence` compile hook. The [Spec-to-test map](../../DEVELOPERS.md#spec-to-test-map) names the tests behind this spec.

### codeEvidence purpose

Architecture and technical review shards cite **repo source files** as evidence. At compile time, the hook:

1. Resolves **line ranges** from link text (for example `L6-L8`, `lines 12–15`, `:42`)
2. Resolves **symbols** from the URL fragment (`file.ts#symbol`) or from the link label when no fragment is present, such as ``[`countItems`](../../src/counts.ts)``
3. Appends GitHub-style **`#L` fragments** (`#L6`, `#L6-L8`) to the link target
4. Rewrites the target path to be relative to the guide's [link base](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#when-it-runs)

The publish-relative pass then rebases the `../` links whose path the hook leaves as the shard wrote it, against the same link base. Such a link can lead to a Markdown file or to another path the hook doesn't read, like `.nvmrc`. It can also lead to a source file that the hook doesn't find, even when the hook added a line fragment to it. In `DEVELOPERS.md`, the hook rebases `../../package.json` to `package.json`, and the publish-relative pass rebases `../../.nvmrc` to `.nvmrc`. [Publish-relative exclusions](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#publish-relative-exclusions) lists the links that pass leaves alone, a link the hook rebased among them.

### codeEvidence link matching

A link is rewritten when **all** of the following hold:

- Standard markdown link syntax: `[label](path)`
- Target path names a **file in the repository**: one with a code or data extension like `.ts` or `.yaml`, or a path with no `.` in it like `Makefile`
- Target is not `http://`, `https://`, or `#…`
- The link is outside fenced code and code spans

Markdown (`.md`) links, external URLs, and same-guide shard links are left unchanged.

The hook skips a path to an extensionless file when the path has a `.` anywhere in it, such as `../../Makefile` or `./Makefile`. A line range in the label of such a link doesn't add an `#L` fragment. The publish-relative pass still rebases the `../` path.

The hook finds fenced code and code spans as the [link passes](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/link-passes.md) do, and it reads a label and a target as they do. It reads each run of lines between two fences at once, so a label outside code can still wrap onto the next line, and an unfinished link such as `[x](see` doesn't take in a link on the next line. In a label that contains an image, such as a linked image's, the hook reads a line range or a symbol only from the text outside the image.

**Code and data differ in what the hook adds.** A code file can be cited by line, so symbol lookup can give it an `#L` fragment. A data file, such as configuration or records, is resolved and rebased for the output path. It gets an `#L` fragment only from a line range the shard writes in the label, the path or the fragment, because symbol lookup runs for code files only. Link validation uses the same code and data extension lists. To look symbols up in a data format, list its extension in `lint.codeExtensions`. See [Built-in link validation](../../docs/features/link-validation.md).

### codeEvidence line ranges

Line ranges are parsed from the **link label** first, then from the path (before any `#` fragment). The hook always emits GitHub-style **`#L…` fragments** (protocol output — not localized).

**Language-neutral forms** (always recognized):

| Form in label or path | Fragment           |
| --------------------- | ------------------ |
| `L6-L8`, `L6–L8`      | `#L6-L8`           |
| `L42`                 | `#L42`             |
| `:10-20`, `:10`       | `#L10-L20`, `#L10` |
| bare `1-2`            | `#L1-L2`           |

**Locale word forms** come from the active [locale pack](#locale-pack) (`lineRangeWords`). Default **en-US** recognizes `line` / `lines` (case-insensitive), for example `line 42` → `#L42` and `lines 12–15` → `#L12-L15`. Other locales may supply different authored words; they are not MDCP protocol vocabulary. See [Locale and language boundary](../../docs/features/design-constraints/locale-and-language.md).

If the URL already has a line fragment such as `#L6` or `#L6-L8`, the hook keeps it and writes each `l` in it as `L`, so `#l6-l8` becomes `#L6-L8`.

### codeEvidence symbols

When no line range is found:

1. If the URL has a `#fragment` that is not already `#L…`, treat the fragment as a **symbol name** and look it up in the resolved source file.
2. Otherwise, treat the **link label** as the symbol (backticks and surrounding whitespace stripped).

Symbol lookup links the first line where the symbol appears as a whole word. That line can be an import, a call or a comment above the declaration. To cite the declaration, write its line range in the label or the fragment. Lookup runs for code files only, and a data file skips both steps.

When neither step finds a line, the hook drops the `#fragment`, and the link points at the whole file.

### codeEvidence path resolution

The hook finds the source file in the order [Path lookup order](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/path-lookup-order.md) gives for `codeEvidence`. When a source file is resolved, the hook rewrites the link target to a POSIX path relative to the guide's [link base](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#when-it-runs), preserving any `#L…` fragment added by the hook. You don't configure the hook for this. It resolves a shard-relative path as written, then rebases it to that link base.

When no directory has the file, the path stays as written, and the [line range](#codeevidence-line-ranges) rules still set the fragment. The hook keeps an existing `#L` fragment, and otherwise adds one from a line range in the label or path. Symbol lookup has no file to scan, so without a line range the hook drops any other `#fragment`.

### codeEvidence exclusions

The hook **does not** transform:

- Markdown shard links (`.md`)
- External URLs
- Link syntax in fenced code or in a code span
- The path of a source link whose file can't be resolved (see [codeEvidence path resolution](#codeevidence-path-resolution) for its fragment)
- A symbol in a data-file link into an `#L` fragment, unless the extension is listed in `lint.codeExtensions`
- Body text when `codeEvidence` is disabled via `compile.hooks: { "codeEvidence": false }` or an explicit hook override that omits it

### codeEvidence config

Path rewriting rebases each path to the guide's link base, the file being assembled: its compiled guide or the monolith. Runs by default, so an empty `compile` keeps it on:

```json
{
  "name": "architecture-review",
  "path": "review",
  "compile": {}
}
```

`compile.outputFile` publishes the guide to a path you choose, and the hook rebases each path to that file. The path resolves relative to `outputDir`. With `outputDir: "_build"` and the docs root at `docs/`, `"../../architecture-review.md"` is a file at the repository root. Set `compile.scopeRoot` too when the guide stitches shards outside its directory, or cites files that resolve only from that root. The [linked-shard walk](../../docs/features/manifest-compile-order.md#linked-shards-and-the-file-name-fallback) keeps a shard under it, and evidence lookup tries it last, as [Path lookup order](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/path-lookup-order.md) says. `compile.scopeRoot` resolves from the docs root, and `"."` is the docs root itself:

```json
{
  "name": "architecture-review",
  "path": "review",
  "compile": {
    "scopeRoot": ".",
    "outputFile": "../../architecture-review.md"
  }
}
```

Opt out: `"hooks": { "codeEvidence": false }`. See [Default compile hooks](../../docs/features/default-compile-hooks.md).

### codeEvidence compile example

Shard input (`docs/review/claim.md`): <!-- mdcp-paths: illustrative -->

```markdown
Evidence: [`countItems`](../../src/counts.ts)

See [access.rules L6-L8](../../config/access.rules).
```

Compiled output, when the first line of `src/counts.ts` with the word `countItems` is line 6 and the guide's output is `architecture-review.md` at the repository root: <!-- mdcp-paths: illustrative -->

```markdown
Evidence: [`countItems`](src/counts.ts#L6)

See [access.rules L6-L8](config/access.rules#L6-L8).
```

<!-- mdcp-shard: end ../../docs/client-core/compile-hooks/code-evidence.md -->

<!-- mdcp-shard: start ../../docs/client-core/compile-hooks/inline-inserts.md -->

## inlineInserts

Specification for the `inlineInserts` compile hook. The [Spec-to-test map](../../DEVELOPERS.md#spec-to-test-map) names the tests behind this spec.

### inlineInserts purpose

Guides link to **captioned insert shards** (`.md` files) in typed libraries under the docs root. Shard bodies may be markdown tables, prose, or **media embeds** (images, video, audio). At compile time, the hook:

1. Inlines insert markdown at the **first** link (per guide, per file)
2. Adds a numbered **`####` heading** (GFM only — no HTML, no directives)
3. Rewrites **later** links to the same file as markdown back-links (`[label](#slug)`)

### inlineInserts layout

One library directory per insert type (library-science convention):

```text
docs/
  diagrams/              # flow charts, sequence diagrams (markdown tables or images)
  tables/                # reference tables, comparison matrices
  figures/               # screenshots, static diagrams
  media/                 # video, audio, and other captioned media embeds
  inserts/               # optional generic captioned blocks
  review/
    insert-catalog.md    # links to ../diagrams/…, ../tables/…, ../figures/…, ../media/…
```

Link targets are always `.md` insert shards. Put binary assets alongside the shard (or under the same library) and reference them from the shard body with `![Overview](./component-map.png)` or an HTML `<video>` / `<audio>` block when your renderer supports it.

Shards link with normal markdown — no `<!-- directives -->`.

### inlineInserts link matching

A link is an insert reference when **all** of the following hold:

- Inline link syntax, `[label](path)`, with the label and target read as the [link passes](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/link-passes.md) read them. An image, `![alt](path)`, isn't an insert reference.
- Target starts with an insert library directory and a `/`, after an optional `./` or run of `../`. The directories are `diagram`, `diagrams`, `table`, `tables`, `figure`, `figures`, `media`, `insert` and `inserts`, in any case. No `http://` or `https://` URL starts that way.
- The path after the directory doesn't start with `#` or whitespace. It ends in `.md` in any case, with at least one character before the `.md`.
- An optional `#fragment` after the `.md` can't be empty, and file lookup ignores it.

The hook reads the whole shard body, fenced code and code spans included. So it inlines an insert, or writes a back-link, for an insert link in a code example too, where the [link passes](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/link-passes.md) leave a link as written.

### inlineInserts exclusions

The hook **does not** transform:

- Regular shard links, such as `./intro.md` or `../glossary/term.md` <!-- mdcp-paths: illustrative -->
- Direct links to binary assets such as `../figures/architecture.png` or `../figures/demo.mp4`; see [layout](#inlineinserts-layout)
- External URLs, even when the path contains `diagrams/`
- Links to missing insert files (left unchanged)
- Body text when `inlineInserts` is disabled via `compile.hooks: { "inlineInserts": false }` or an explicit hook override that omits it

### inlineInserts first inline

The first reference to an insert file (document order across all shards in the guide) is replaced with:

```markdown
#### {Kind} {n}. {caption}

{insert shard body — tables, prose, images, video, audio, …}
```

- **Kind** — `Diagram`, `Table`, `Figure`, `Media`, or `Insert` (from parent library directory)
- **n** — serial number for that kind in this guide (see **Numbered captions** below)
- **caption** — link label, or a humanized basename when the label is empty
- **Anchor slug** — GitHub-style slug of the full heading (for example `Table 1. Status codes` → `#table-1-status-codes`)

The label of a linked image, `[![I](./i.png)](../diagrams/d.md)`, contains the image. The heading then reads `#### Diagram 1. ![I](./i.png)`, and a back-link to it uses the slug of that text, `#diagram-1-iipng`.

Output uses GFM headings and back-links for captions. The hook inlines each shard body as written. The assembly passes after the hooks then treat that body as part of the shard, from link rewriting to [table re-alignment](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/tables-after-link-rewriting.md). A body can contain markdown tables and `![images](…)`.

The heading and body replace the link, so a first reference in a table cell breaks the table, as the [compile example](#inlineinserts-compile-example) shows. Give the first reference a paragraph of its own, ahead of any table cell that links to the insert.

In the compiled markdownlint pass of [`mdcp check`](../../docs/features/check-gate.md#check-gate-stages), the broken row fails MD056 (table-column-count). That pass lints only the outputs that the globs in its `lint.markdownlint.compiledConfig` file match, and a table broken in any other output passes the check.

### inlineInserts numbered captions

Serial counters are **per insert kind** and **per guide compile**:

| Kind    | First inline heading example   | Second inline (same kind) |
| ------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| diagram | `#### Diagram 1. Request flow` | `#### Diagram 2. …`       |
| table   | `#### Table 1. Status codes`   | `#### Table 2. …`         |
| figure  | `#### Figure 1. Component map` | `#### Figure 2. …`        |
| media   | `#### Media 1. Walkthrough`    | `#### Media 2. …`         |

Rules:

- Diagram and table counters are independent (`Diagram 1` then `Table 1` then `Diagram 2` is valid)
- Counters continue across shards via shared per-guide hook state
- Each guide starts at 1 for each kind (two guides sharing one insert file each get their own `Diagram 1`)
- Repeat links to an **already inlined file** do not consume a new number (back-link only)

### inlineInserts deduplication

Within one guide:

- First link to `../diagrams/flow.md` → inline under numbered heading <!-- mdcp-paths: illustrative -->
- Later links to the same resolved file (any path spelling, with or without `#fragment`) → `` `[label](#diagram-1-…)` ``
- Same basename in different libraries (`diagrams/overview.md` vs `tables/overview.md`) → separate headings and anchors <!-- mdcp-paths: illustrative -->

### inlineInserts path resolution

The hook finds each insert shard in the order [Path lookup order](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/path-lookup-order.md) gives for `inlineInserts`.

### inlineInserts config

Runs by default. Optional search roots, each the parent of an insert library directory such as `diagrams/`:

```json
{
  "name": "architecture-review",
  "compile": {
    "hooksConfig": {
      "inlineInserts": { "searchRoots": ["shared"] }
    }
  }
}
```

A link to `diagrams/flow.md` that no earlier root in the [lookup order](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/path-lookup-order.md) resolves then finds `shared/diagrams/flow.md`. <!-- mdcp-paths: illustrative -->

Opt out: `"hooks": { "inlineInserts": false }`. See [Default compile hooks](../../docs/features/default-compile-hooks.md).

### inlineInserts compile example

Shard input:

```markdown
| Insert                                      | Summary     |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| [Request flow](../diagrams/request-flow.md) | Client path |

See [Request flow](../diagrams/request-flow.md) again in prose.
```

Compiled fragment (first guide mention), with trailing spaces trimmed. The header and delimiter rows keep the shard's widths, and the insert splits the row with the link:

```text
| Insert                                      | Summary     |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
|

#### Diagram 1. Request flow

| Step | Actor  |
| ---- | ------ |
| 1    | Client |

 | Client path |

See [Request flow](#diagram-1-request-flow) again in prose.
```

Example fixture: [`examples/sample-guides/inserts-demo/`](../../examples/sample-guides/inserts-demo). Its catalog gives each insert's first reference a paragraph of its own, and its table links to each insert again. Compile turns those table links into back-links and re-aligns the table. See [GitHub media reference](../../examples/sample-guides/inserts-demo/github-media-help.md) for a format matrix (PNG, JPEG, GIF, SVG, MP4, MP3/WAV, Mermaid, tables, lists) and minimal generated sample assets under `figures/` and `media/`.

**Figure with embedded image** (shard `figures/component-map.md`): <!-- mdcp-paths: illustrative -->

```markdown
![Component map overview](./component-map.png)
```

Catalog link `` `[Component map](../figures/component-map.md)` `` compiles to a numbered `#### Figure 1. …` heading followed by that image markdown.

**Media with embedded video** (shard `media/walkthrough.md`): <!-- mdcp-paths: illustrative -->

```markdown
<video src="./walkthrough.mp4" controls></video>
```

Catalog link `` `[Walkthrough](../media/walkthrough.md)` `` compiles to `#### Media 1. Walkthrough` followed by the video embed.

<!-- mdcp-shard: end ../../docs/client-core/compile-hooks/inline-inserts.md -->

## ignoreGuides

**`ignoreGuides`** is a list of guide names on the **compiling** guide, under `compile.crossGuideLinks.ignoreGuides`. Cross-guide links to a listed guide keep pointing at the source shard instead of rewriting to a `#slug` target. A link to a shard the compiling guide stitches can still take its in-document anchor. [Same compiled output preference](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/cross-guide-links.md#same-compiled-output-preference) says when the cross-guide pass gives it one. [`ignoreGuides` interaction](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/publish-relative-links.md#ignoreguides-interaction) says how compile rebases a kept path, and when a `./` or bare link to a stitched shard takes `#slug`. The listed guide stays in `compileOrder` and in the link index.

Read [Cross-guide link rewriting](../../docs/features/compile-pipeline/cross-guide-links.md) for how other links rewrite, and the [publish-only link policy](../../docs/features/link-validation.md#publish-only-link-policy) for how link validation treats kept shard paths.

<!-- mdcp-shard: end ../../docs/glossary/ignore-guides.md -->

<!-- mdcp-shard: start ../../docs/glossary/locale-pack.md -->

## locale pack

A **locale pack** is MDCP’s compile-time bundle of natural-language data that is **not** GFM protocol shape. It covers:

- **Generated wording**: text such as US-English insert captions (`Table 1. …`) and `BROKEN LINK` marker copy
- **Locale-specific patterns**: optional heading-key patterns for semantic refs
- **Parse-input word cues**: authored words a compile hook may recognize (such as en-US `line` / `lines` for [codeEvidence](#codeevidence) line ranges)
- **Preamble heading title**: a title such as en-US `About this guide` for strip/promote defaults (`aboutThisGuideTitle`)

Default `en-US` (one BCP 47 JSON file per locale under `src/locale/locales/`). Language-neutral markup forms and GitHub-style `#L…` fragment **output** stay outside the pack.

<!-- mdcp-shard: end ../../docs/glossary/locale-pack.md -->

<!-- mdcp-shard: start ../../docs/glossary/authored-gfm.md -->

## authored GFM

Shard markdown as written before compile, with no preprocessor substitution or template conditionals. Compile hooks may transform it during assembly. Read [Preprocessor / templating (out of scope)](../../docs/features/design-constraints/preprocessor-templating.md#preprocessor--templating-out-of-scope).

<!-- mdcp-shard: end ../../docs/glossary/authored-gfm.md -->
